title: Review: Aseptic technique and microbial culture; Population growth and interactions
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Eduqas A-level Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: EC03a#t3 term and clue written for the game; EC03a#t4 term and clue written for the game; EC03b#t1 term and clue written for the game; PR04b#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: EC03a#N.2a, EC03b#N.2, PR04a#N.5, PR04b#N.11, EC03a#N.5a, EC03b#N.9b, PR04a#N.11, PR04b#N.4, EC03a#N.9, EC03b#N.12. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Density-dependent factor
items.clue: Affects a larger proportion of a population the more crowded it is, e.g. disease

items.label: Density-independent factor
items.clue: Affects a similar proportion however crowded the population, e.g. frost or flood

items.label: Intraspecific competition
items.clue: Rivalry between members of one kind of organism, which need exactly the same resources

items.label: Death phase
items.clue: Last of the four stages of a closed culture, when the number of living bacteria falls.

questions.stem: A newt population starts the year at 500. During the year there are 120 births, 80 deaths, 15 immigrants and 35 emigrants. What is the population at the end of the year?
Why does competition occur between members of the same population?

options.text: It does not occur: members of one species share their resources, and competition arises only between different species.
It occurs only when two individuals confront each other over the same item of food, the same mate or the same nesting site.
It occurs only in solitary species, because individuals living together in a group are by definition cooperating.
Individuals of one species have identical needs, so when a resource is scarce what one uses leaves less for others.

questions.explanation: Members of a population need exactly the same food, water, light, space, mates or nest sites. Whenever such a resource is in limited supply, each individual's consumption reduces the amount available to the rest.

questions.stem: A student adds 1.0 cm³ of a bacterial culture to 9.0 cm³ of sterile water and mixes. She transfers 1.0 cm³ of this into a second 9.0 cm³ of sterile water, and repeats until she has made four dilutions. What fraction of the original concentration of bacteria is in the fourth dilution?
questions.explanation: Each step is 1 cm³ in a total of 10 cm³, a factor of 10. Four steps: 10⁴ = 10 000, so 10⁻⁴ of the original.

questions.stem: A student records the size of a duckweed population every two days and plots it on a logarithmic vertical axis against time on a non-logarithmic horizontal axis. Which observation would show that growth was exponential?

options.text: The points form a curve that becomes steeper with time, as exponential growth does on ordinary axes.
The points lie on a straight line, because a fixed number of plants was added in each two-day interval.
The points trace an S-shaped curve, because all populations grow according to the sigmoid model.
The points lie on a straight line, because the population multiplied by the same factor in each two-day interval.

questions.stem: Yeast was grown in a sealed flask of glucose solution and cell counts were made every four hours. After 24 hours the count stopped rising. Which explanation for the plateau is correct?

options.text: The yeast cells have all stopped dividing, and none of them are dying, so the count stays the same.
Natality now equals mortality, because glucose has become scarce and ethanol has accumulated.
The plateau is reached only at the moment when the glucose in the flask has been completely used up.
The flask has reached the carrying capacity that applies to yeast in any environment.

questions.stem: When a competing species is removed from a habitat, the population of the remaining species often increases. Which statement best explains why?

options.text: Individuals reproduce faster because the species needs to fill the space the competitor left.
Food and other resources are shared among fewer individuals, so births rise or deaths fall.
The competitor had been eating the remaining species, so fewer of its individuals now die.
With no competitor, the population is no longer limited and would go on growing without end.

questions.stem: A student plans to test three disinfectants on a lawn of bacteria in Petri dishes. Which plan for incubating the dishes follows safe aseptic practice?

options.text: Tape the lid with two short strips and incubate the dish upside down at 25 °C.
Seal the lid all the way round with tape and incubate the dish lid-side up at 25 °C.
Tape the lid with two short strips and incubate the dish upside down at 37 °C for faster growth.
Tape the lid with two short strips, incubate upside down at 25 °C, and lift the lid daily to check.

questions.explanation: Two strips hold the lid on but let air in, discouraging anaerobic pathogens. Upside down stops condensation dripping; 25 °C avoids favouring human pathogens.

questions.stem: A student spreads 0.2 cm³ of the 10⁻³ dilution of a culture onto agar. After incubation there are 86 colonies. What is the number of living cells per cm³ in the original culture?
A storm kills 30% of a seabird colony. Over the following years, the colony returns to its former size. Which explanation is correct?

options.text: The storm was a density-dependent factor, because it killed so many birds in a colony as large as this one was.
Density-dependent factors can only ever reduce populations, so the recovery afterwards must have been due to density-independent factors.
The recovery shows that the carrying capacity is fixed by the birds' breeding rate rather than by the environment.
The storm was density-independent; reduced competition afterwards let natality exceed mortality until carrying capacity was regained.

questions.stem: A forester plants beech seedlings very close together in a cleared plot with no other plant species. Over ten years, most of the seedlings die and the survivors are tall and spaced out. Which explanation is best?

options.text: With no other species in the plot, there was no competition, so the deaths must have had an abiotic cause.
The seedlings that died gave up their place so that the strongest could grow, which benefits the species.
Competition could only have occurred where the seedlings' branches or roots were seen to touch.
Intraspecific competition: seedlings with identical needs shade each other, and the shaded ones die.
